cells.tense: You are standing where what arrives meets your choosing, and you know the turning is yours.
cells.act: close the cycle and leave the door open for the next
cells.ask: Bring the task still sitting one step short of done to its close this week, then keep the space after it unblocked for whatever follows.
cells.core:
You are the turning. Not swept by it — you are where each moment comes through, and you can tell the difference because what you meet gets met, not just done to you. Direction is easy from here: you say this, not that, and mean it, and the saying holds because you are present while it happens.

The invitation here is to finish. Something in your hands has been sitting one step short of done — not a big push, the closing move you keep circling. Make it. When it is done, do not seal it shut and do not stand in the doorway; let the cycle close and keep the space after it clear. You arrive and leave at the same time, and that is the work this reading is pointing at.
cells.sheetLine: You close it clean and leave the next door open.

cells.tense: You are bracing for what has not arrived yet, and the current chooses while you brace.
cells.act: complete it without making it final
cells.ask: Walk one task already under your hand to its last step, then leave it finished without deciding what comes next.
cells.core:
You can feel the next thing coming before it lands, and your body is already there. Meeting turns into pre-empting past a certain point: every unopened door gets a plan, and the cause of what happens keeps landing somewhere you are not. Freshness becomes a forecast you brace against instead of timing you read.

The tighter version: take one task already under your hand — not the coming one — and walk it to its last step. Complete it without making it final. Do not announce what it leads to, do not close it so hard it seals against the next cycle. End it and leave air around the ending. That is how timing comes back into your grip: you do the piece within reach, and the rest arrives when it does.
cells.sheetLine: You're bracing at a door before it's been opened.

cells.tense: You are still at a door that closed behind you, waiting for what already crossed.
cells.act: let the finished thing be the start of something
cells.ask: Take something in your life that is quietly over and let what it became count as a beginning, even unnamed.
cells.core:
Nothing new lands because the last thing is still on the table. Not stubbornness — you have been holding a state that felt right, and turning from it looks like losing it. So the moment keeps arriving and keeps sliding past, and direction stays with whoever is moving, which is not you right now.

This returns through what you have left in a drawer. Something in your life is already finished — a chapter, a stretch of your own, a version of you — and instead of releasing it you have kept it open, refusing the outcome. Let the finished thing be the start of something. Not a whole new direction; the recognition that it can be both: over, and the ground the next thing stands on. Arriving gets easier when you stop holding the last arrival shut.
cells.sheetLine: The door behind you is still open, and nothing new gets through.

cells.tense: You are steering without knowing you hold the wheel, and the pattern turns on its own.
cells.act: decide from what is here now, not from habit
cells.ask: Name the next act before you do it, and choose it from what is actually here, not from what you usually do.
cells.core:
Things arrive and you respond, and at some point the response stopped being a choice. Not a failure — the movements got practiced, and practiced movements do not announce themselves. You meet each moment on the way past, so the pattern reads as circumstance. The consequence shows up later and lands as a surprise, because the part of you that aimed it was not paying attention.

Put your hand on the wheel for one turn. Name the next act before you do it — not the whole direction, just this one — and decide it from what is actually here, not from what you usually do. The difference shows immediately: choosing has a texture that repeating does not. Do it once and the turning is yours again, because it was the whole time.
cells.sheetLine: You're steering, and nobody told you your hands were on the wheel.

attempts.check: Rule 8 first. The unsupported claim is in the Too Much and Unacknowledged cells: I describe a person who is carried by things arriving, repeating patterns without noticing, with the cause located somewhere else. The record supports the mechanism (the turning unrecognized, authorship handed to the current), but it does not support claiming the person's history, what they have tried, or that they are 'surprised' at consequences. A reader could reasonably say: this is not my life, I know exactly what I am choosing. So the asks stay small and structural, not diagnostic; they survive being wrong because finishing one waiting thing costs nothing if the read misses. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line that makes the portal sound like an event that happens to someone. Cut those. The medicine acts are the person's own, so no one else is needed anywhere in this quartet.
